_comment: Mutations that re-introduce the FABRICATED ORACLE, one at a time.
Every mutation must be caught by the tests in this spec's pytest target:
tests/test_oracle_availability.py         -- the server must report the REAL state
tests/test_pwa_oracle_honesty.py           -- the PWA must not fabricate one
tests/test_oracle_confidence_threshold.py  -- the threshold must not vanish
tests/test_web_oracle_honesty.py           -- the WEB client must not fabricate one
The fiction being re-introduced, in its original form:
const canUseOracle = true; // Oracle is available to everyone
const [oracleConfidence, setOracleConfidence] = useState(95);
const regime = parseInt(formData.oracleRegime || "1", 10);
const confidence = formData.oracleConfidence || 95;
on a deployment whose api container logs, once per worker:
WARNING [api.simulation_router:122] - Oracle model not found at
/app/data/oracle_model.joblib
AND, just as bad, the SILENT weakening of the guard:
min_confidence_raw = (self.symbol_selection_config.oracle_confidence or 0.0)
... if s.get("oracle_confidence", 0.0) >= min_confidence
which turned a '>= 0.95' filter into '>= 0.0' -- a filter that admits
EVERY symbol, with nothing said about it.
The server-side mutants matter as much as the client-side ones: a hard-coded
False in the endpoint would also 'pass' the unavailable case while keeping
the oracle switched off forever. Both directions are pinned.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/oracle_availability_truth.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the server says the oracle is NEVER available (a constant False)
mutations.replace: return False  # MUTANT: the oracle is never available

mutations.label: B: the server says the oracle is ALWAYS available (a constant True)
mutations.replace: return True  # MUTANT: the oracle is always available

mutations.label: C: the endpoint ignores the server and always answers False
D: the endpoint ignores the server and always answers True
E: the endpoint FAILS OPEN when the probe errors
F: the PWA hard-codes the oracle as available again
mutations.replace: const canUseOracle = true; // MUTANT: Oracle is available to everyone

mutations.label: G: the PWA defaults the oracle confidence back to 95
H: the PWA launch payload invents a 95% confidence again
I: the PWA launch payload invents oracle regime 1 again
J: the strategy editor preselects oracle regime 1 again
mutations.replace: value={oracleRegime !== null && oracleRegime !== undefined ? String(oracleRegime) : "1"} // MUTANT

mutations.label: K: the PWA switches the symbol-selection mode behind the customer's back
mutations.replace: if (false) { // MUTANT: the mode is substituted instead

mutations.label: L: the SERVER reads an absent or zero confidence as NO threshold
mutations.needle:
if raw is None or raw <= 0:
        return DEFAULT_ORACLE_CONFIDENCE_PERCENT / 100.0
mutations.replace:
if raw is None or raw <= 0:
        return 0.0  # MUTANT: 'not chosen' becomes 'no threshold'

mutations.label: M: the SERVER's declared threshold is changed (a new number, silently)
mutations.replace: DEFAULT_ORACLE_CONFIDENCE_PERCENT: float = 50.0  # MUTANT: a new threshold value

mutations.label: N: the server keeps claiming a model whose file has been deleted
mutations.replace: if False and isinstance(loaded, _LoadedOracle) and not loaded.path.exists():

mutations.label: O: the server-side default assumes the oracle exists again
mutations.replace: use_oracle: bool = True  # MUTANT: the old assumption

mutations.label: P: the WEB client invents a 95% confidence threshold again
mutations.replace: const defaultConfidence = 95; // MUTANT: the client invents a threshold

mutations.label: Q: the WEB client stops asking the server what it can do
mutations.replace: const { data: capabilities } = { data: { oracleAvailable: true } }; // MUTANT: nobody asked

mutations.label: R: the WEB client decides the oracle's availability from the customer's plan
mutations.replace: const canUseOracle = oracleEntitled; // MUTANT: the plan decides the availability
